o: Every cell must equal the cell below it (so each column is constant) and differ from the cell to its right (so adjacent columns differ). Checking all cells directly against both neighbors verifies the conditions; with m, n ≤ 10 brute force is instant. Example [[1,0,2],[1,0,2]] passes: columns are constant and adjacent columns differ. [[1,1,1],[0,0,0]] fails the horizontal rule; [[1],[2],[3]] fails the vertical rule.
k: Column-constancy plus adjacent-column-difference fully characterize valid grids.
One pass checking right and down neighbors per cell suffices.
Checking each cell once (not both directions) avoids redundant work but either way is correct.

a.i: Iterate all cells; fail fast if the cell below differs or the cell to the right is equal. Every constraint is local, so a single scan decides the answer.
s: If i+1 < m and grid[i][j] != grid[i+1][j], return false.
If j+1 < n and grid[i][j] == grid[i][j+1], return false.

w: Watch the asymmetry: vertical requires equality, horizontal requires inequality — swapping them is the typical slip. Single-row and single-column grids exercise each rule independently. Follow-up: count the minimum changes to satisfy the conditions (per-column value voting), or extend to diagonal constraints.
